solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Function is reversed in dry fruit

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a cone is the dry woody fruit of a conifer

indicators.note: reversed tells us the little word is in the clue is to be read backwards

explanation.surface: A mathematical function is somehow turned backwards inside a piece of dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: A pine cone counts as a dry fruit botanically, which makes 'dry fruit' a fair if unusual clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosine is a trigonometric function, one of the standard ratios of an angle.

clue.text: Chap not curious about English monument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reworked letters go round the abbreviation
curious means odd, so these letters come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A man who isn't curious about an English monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' reworks CHAP NOT into CNOTAPH, and 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial, a monument to those buried elsewhere.

clue.text: Extraordinary character, fantastic Orpheus rescuing queen

indicators.note: rescuing means taking in and holding, so the reworked letters hold the royal abbreviation
fantastic means fanciful, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: The mythical Orpheus heroically rescues a queen from the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' scrambles the hero's name and 'rescuing' has it take in the queen; ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero is a fictional figure with extraordinary powers, a remarkable character.

clue.text: Something possibly common in journo, unfortunately

indicators.note: in means the word sits inside the run of letters journo unfortunately

explanation.surface: A journalist unfortunately writes something rather common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' looks like vulgar, but a common one is the grammar kind, as opposed to a proper one.
explanation.definitionFit: A common noun names a general class of things, so a noun may be common.

clue.text: Male relative back in rut, still

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
nan is a grandmother, a relative

indicators.note: back in points to the final letter of the word rut

explanation.surface: A male family member has gone backwards and is stuck in a rut, unmoving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in rut' gives only the last letter, T. 'Rut' tempts as the stag's mating season, but here it only donates a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still, not flowing or moving.

clue.text: Tool didn't used to be gripping one from below

indicators.note: from below means read upwards in a down entry, so backwards
gripping means holding, so the contraction holds the number word

parts.note: wasn't is the past negative of to be

explanation.surface: A tool that was once held from underneath, but no longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' gives WASNONET and 'from below' reads it upwards, as a down entry does.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small fine-toothed saw used for cutting joints in woodwork.

clue.text: Gone off to collect very old friend that's come up, don't be late!

indicators.note: to collect means to gather in, so the reworked letters hold the other pieces
off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
come up in a down entry means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Having left to pick up a very old friend, one urges promptness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' reworks GONE as GEON; 'that's come up' turns VOMATE into ETAMOV, which 'to collect' puts after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a move on is an idiom urging someone to hurry up so as not to be late.

clue.text: A maiden untrue

parts.note: a miss is an unmarried young woman, a maiden

explanation.surface: A young woman who is unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or awry, not right, so untrue in the sense of out of true.

clue.text: Difficult linking rings really, at first

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the joining word goes round a letter

parts.note: tying means joining or linking

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word really

explanation.surface: Linking rings together is really hard, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' is the containment signal, not a noun: TYING goes round R from 'really, at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means testing one's patience, hard to deal with.

clue.text: My bottles to consume, nourishing

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside as in a bottle, so the possessive goes round

parts.note: to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: Someone's bottles are there for drinking, and nourishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' is a verb here, meaning holds inside, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaty food is substantial and filling, full of protein.

clue.text: Record air on new planet

indicators.note: on means the record and air sit after the new letter, built onto it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A recording of a melody is made about a newly discovered planet.
explanation.walkthrough: EP for an extended-play record is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the eighth planet from the sun in our solar system.

clue.text: In smart manner, girl talking?

indicators.note: talking signals that the girl's name is spoken and we hear its sound

parts.note: Natalie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a girl who dresses smartly is chatting away.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name NATALIE, said out loud, sounds very close to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nattily means smartly or dapperly, as of someone neatly dressed.

clue.text: Opportunity to switch

definitions.meaning: a go or chance in sequence, as in waiting one's go
to change direction or change over

explanation.surface: A chance to change course.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is one's go in a sequence, and to turn is to swivel or change direction.

clue.text: Man soon set to train as builder

indicators.note: to train is to shape or direct, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A man will soon begin training to become a builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is the anagram signal for MAN SOON SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a craftsman who builds with cut stone, a kind of builder.

clue.text: Stop bear though

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it
still can mean nevertheless or though

explanation.surface: Stop, even though it is hard to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt, a situation where all movement has stopped.

clue.text: Quite insignificant touring car at the back

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the trivial word surrounds the picked letter

parts.note: petty means trivial or insignificant

indicators.note: at the back points to the final letter of the word car

explanation.surface: A minor car tour with a car tagged on behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the back' takes R from car, and 'touring' puts PETTY round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty as an adverb means fairly or quite, as in pretty good.

clue.text: Where one's served meals, really on wheels

indicators.note: on means the intensifier is placed after the vehicle, built onto it

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
very and really are both intensifiers

explanation.surface: A place serving meals that is literally on wheels, like a food truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' is informal slang for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a restaurant where roast meat is carved and served to diners.

clue.text: Horrid being rebellious

explanation.surface: Horrid behaviour from a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting means disgusting, and also taking part in a revolt against rulers.

clue.text: Mobile phone carrying label, particular shape

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the reworked letters hold the label word
mobile means moving, so the letters move about

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A mobile phone with a label stuck on it, in a particular shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' is not the device here: it scrambles the next word, which 'carrying' wraps round the label.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptagon is a specific polygon, a plane figure with seven sides.

clue.text: Duo allowed in band

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means permitted or allowed

explanation.surface: A pair permitted to join a musical band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' is not a group of musicians but a ring worn on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band or chain worn round the wrist.

clue.text: Dog clue

definitions.meaning: a breed of gun dog that stands still to indicate game

explanation.surface: A hint about a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a hunting dog breed, and a pointer is also a hint or tip.

clue.text: You finished eating meal finally after seconds

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the abbreviation
eating means taking in, so the ended word holds a letter

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word meal

explanation.surface: Someone has finished a meal after taking second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives L from meal; 'eating' puts OVER round it, after S. 'You' is the definition because the reader is the one solving.
explanation.definitionFit: You, the reader working through this crossword, are the person cracking its clues.

clue.text: Irritable passenger in the end picked up by driver

indicators.note: picked up by means taken in by, so the driver holds the letter

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word passenger

explanation.surface: A grumpy fare who was finally collected by the taxi driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' gives R from passenger, which 'picked up by' puts inside CABBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means bad-tempered and grumpy.

clue.text: Funny snap

explanation.surface: A funny photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a joke or quip, and to crack is to break sharply.

clue.text: Sorry poet, I suspect, in store

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful, so these letters are not trusted in their order and get reworked

explanation.surface: An apologetic poet suspects something is kept in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' is the anagram signal for SORRY POET plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where things are kept or stored.

clue.text: A toothy thing standing to bite unknown Italian food

indicators.note: to bite means to hold in the teeth, so the turned word grips the letter
standing means upright, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: a zip has interlocking teeth
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: Something with teeth standing up to bite into an unknown Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns the zip upwards, as a down entry reads, and 'to bite' grips Z; the A that opens the clue ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizza is a well-known Italian dish of baked dough with toppings.

clue.text: United Nations berating lots of countries, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: The UN is scolding many countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United Nations' here is not the UN but any group of nations acting together.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of countries united by shared interests.

clue.text: Old language in newspaper, Serbian

indicators.note: in means the word sits inside the run of letters newspaper Serbian

explanation.surface: An old language turns up in a Serbian newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland.

clue.text: Very busy making phone call

definitions.meaning: full of hectic activity, as a lively place is

explanation.surface: A busy person making a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzing place is lively and active, and to buzz someone is slang for to phone them.

clue.text: Warm, sweet drink

definitions.meaning: a fruit-flavoured concentrate diluted with water

explanation.surface: A warm sweet drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means friendly and warm in manner, and a cordial is a sweet fruit concentrate drink.

clue.text: Ludlow's first hurdled by a grey, in labouring horse

indicators.note: being hurdled means being jumped over, so the reworked letters sit on both sides of the picked letter
labouring means struggling, so these letters are worked into a new order
first points to the opening letter of the word Ludlow's

explanation.surface: At Ludlow racecourse a grey horse struggles over the first hurdle.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludlow is an English racecourse. 'labouring' turns A GREY IN into YEARING; 'hurdled by' puts it round L from 'Ludlow's first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse between one and two years old.

clue.text: Peak figure beyond horrendous at the outset

indicators.note: beyond means the number comes after the picked letter
at the outset points to the first letter of the word horrendous

parts.note: eight is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A peak number far beyond anything horrendous seen before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the outset' takes H; 'beyond' places EIGHT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The height of something is its peak or highest point, as in the height of fashion.
